questions.q: Why did the Parsee guide leave the line of the railway and go through the forest?
choices: To stay out of sight of the railway workmen
To gain twenty miles by going straight
To find water and fresh branches for Kiouni
To visit a village where he had family
questions.evidence: they would gain twenty miles by striking directly through the forest

questions.q: What advice from his master did Passepartout follow while riding the bouncing elephant?
choices: To hold tightly to the howdah ropes with both hands
To keep his tongue from getting between his teeth
To close his eyes whenever they went downhill
To sit very still and never look at the ground
questions.evidence: to keep his tongue from between his teeth

questions.q: How did Passepartout behave during the rough ride?
choices: He complained loudly to Mr. Fogg the whole way
He laughed and fed Kiouni pieces of sugar
He grew sick and begged the guide to stop
He slept soundly in spite of all the bouncing
questions.evidence: yet he laughed in the midst of his bouncing

questions.q: When Sir Francis said Kiouni was "made of iron," what did he mean?
choices: The elephant was very strong and tireless
The elephant wore heavy armour for battle
The elephant was stubborn and very hard to steer
The elephant had a cold, unfeeling nature

questions.q: What question worried Passepartout as they rode toward Allahabad?
choices: Whether Fix was secretly following them
What Mr. Fogg would do with the elephant at Allahabad
Whether they had brought enough food for the whole journey
How he would ever replace his lost shoes
questions.evidence: What would Mr. Fogg do with the elephant when he got to Allahabad?

questions.q: Where did the travellers spend the first night?
choices: In a ruined bungalow on the northern slope
In a tent the guide put up beside a spring
In the hut of the elephant's former owner
Up in the howdahs, tied to the elephant's back
questions.evidence: another halt was made on the northern slope, in a ruined bungalow

questions.q: How did Mr. Fogg sleep that night?
choices: Badly, dreaming all night long of the bouncing elephant
Hardly at all, keeping watch for panthers
As peacefully as if he were at home in Saville Row
Only an hour, while he checked his notebook
questions.evidence: he slumbered as peacefully as if he had been in his serene mansion in Saville Row

questions.q: The travellers ate supper "ravenously." What does ravenously mean?
choices: Very slowly
Very hungrily
Very quietly
Very rudely

questions.q: What made the elephant suddenly stop in the thick forest?
choices: A panther crossing the path ahead
The sound of voices and brass instruments
A fallen tree lying right across the narrow path
A river too deep for him to cross
questions.evidence: it now seemed like a distant concert of human voices accompanied by brass instruments

questions.q: What did the guide do when he learned a procession was coming?
choices: Rode the elephant away as fast as he could
Hid the elephant and travellers in a thicket
Went out to ask the passing priests for directions
Climbed a tall tree to watch it go by
questions.evidence: The guide unloosed the elephant and led him into a thicket

questions.q: Who was being carried on the palanquin in the procession?
choices: The body of an old rajah, the young woman's husband
A sick priest being taken to the pagoda of Pillaji
The young woman's father, who led the procession
A rich merchant on his way to Allahabad
questions.evidence: Is that of the prince, her husband

questions.q: Why did the young woman in the procession not seem to resist?
choices: She had agreed to everything of her own free will
She had been drugged with fumes of hemp and opium
She did not know where she was being taken
The guards had promised to set her free later that night
questions.evidence: they had intoxicated her with fumes of hemp and opium

questions.q: Where was the young woman to spend the night?
choices: At the station at Allahabad
In the ruined bungalow on the hill
At the pagoda of Pillaji, two miles away
In the palace of the old rajah of Bundelcund
questions.evidence: To the pagoda of Pillaji, two miles from here

questions.q: What did Fogg suggest just as the guide was about to ride on?
choices: That they hurry to Allahabad before dark
That they save the young woman
That they report what they saw to the governor
That they follow the procession to watch it

questions.q: When Sir Francis called him "a man of heart," how did Fogg reply?
choices: "Never, sir; it is only good sense"
"Sometimes, when I have the time"
"Always, as every Englishman should be"
"Only when there is a wager at stake"
questions.evidence: Sometimes," replied Phileas Fogg, quietly; "when I have the time.

questions.q: What is the most important thing that happens in this chapter?
choices: The elephant runs away and the travellers must walk
Fogg decides to risk his spare time to rescue a woman in danger
The travellers finally reach the station at Allahabad
Passepartout is given the elephant Kiouni as a present
questions.evidence: I have yet twelve hours to spare; I can devote them to that.
